mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT keep edging up from their recent lows, weekday downtown footfall will recover and lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks versus the prior four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -24.3 to -17.7 and TRANSIT improved from -28.7 to -23.6 over the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days while both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue to improve relative to t-1w and t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in RESIDENTIAL staying-home time should suppress discretionary out-of-home shopping, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks relative to the last four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL remains positive at 7.9 to 9.7 while RETAIL_REC stays near -23
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL staying above its prior four-week average.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility rebounds sharply after a depressed week, leisure trips spill into nearby shopping districts within one to two weeks and raise RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 8 points week-on-week from a prior weekly mean below -30
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -22.1 to -32.7 and then -32.0, showing large week-to-week swings
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve within 14 days after a week in which PARKS jumps by at least 8 points from below -30.

mechanism_narrative: If transit access tightens further, retail shopping falls because fewer people can make discretionary trips; a renewed TRANSIT drop should reduce RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -26 after having been above -25 in the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT remains negative and has oscillated between -28.7 and -23.6 in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 28 days after TRANSIT crosses below -26 from a weaker decline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL implies more errand-only and home-centered activity, which displaces leisure shopping and keeps RETAIL_REC below its recent level over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is less negative than RETAIL_REC while RESIDENTIAL stays positive
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves within 7 days even though GROCERY_PHARM rises and RESIDENTIAL stays elevated.

mechanism_narrative: In a commuting-led recovery, gains in WORKPLACES should feed with a one-week lag into retail traffic; if WORKPLACES keeps recovering, RETAIL_REC will be higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -24.3 at t-3w to -17.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays flat or falls over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES continues to trend upward for at least two weekly observations.

mechanism_narrative: A broad leisure rebound across PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM signals higher weekend outing intensity; if both series improve together, retail-and-recreation should rise over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both rise for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both became less negative from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days after both PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM rise for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Under a stable restriction regime, small improvements in mobility are not enough to move retail demand; only when TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain above their recent lows for four weeks will RETAIL_REC recover.
evidence_refs: fact:both series improved modestly but remain well below baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises before both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stay above their t-1w levels for four consecutive weeks.
